labels.name: fresh_produce_and_perishables
labels.definition: Orders primarily requesting fresh fruits, vegetables, meat, fish, dairy, eggs, or bakery items that require refrigeration or spoil quickly.
examples_of_edge_cases: need 2kg tomatoes, a dozen eggs, and fresh basil
can you get me a rotisserie chicken and some sliced deli ham
just want a loaf of the bakery sourdough, still warm if possible
frozen shrimp and a bag of frozen peas please

labels.name: pantry_and_packaged_goods
labels.definition: Orders for shelf-stable groceries such as canned goods, dry pasta, rice, cereal, snacks, condiments, and beverages including soda, juice, coffee, and alcohol.
examples_of_edge_cases: 2 cans of chickpeas, a bag of basmati rice, and some olive oil
grab me a case of sparkling water and a bottle of red wine
protein bars, almonds, and instant oatmeal packets
is the peanut butter on sale, get 2 jars if so

labels.name: household_and_cleaning
labels.definition: Orders for non-food home maintenance items like cleaning sprays, laundry detergent, paper towels, toilet paper, trash bags, and light bulbs.
examples_of_edge_cases: out of dish soap and need more sponges too
pick up a pack of AA batteries and some tin foil
need bleach, but not the scented kind, just regular
toilet paper is almost out, get the big pack

labels.name: personal_care_and_health
labels.definition: Orders for toiletries, cosmetics, over-the-counter medicine, vitamins, and hygiene products intended for personal use on the body.
examples_of_edge_cases: need shampoo and also some ibuprofen for a headache
can you grab feminine pads and a new toothbrush
get the allergy medicine, the non-drowsy one
sunscreen SPF 50 and after-sun lotion please

labels.name: baby_and_pet_supplies
labels.definition: Orders for products intended for infants/toddlers or household pets, including diapers, baby formula, pet food, litter, and pet treats.
examples_of_edge_cases: size 4 diapers and a tub of baby wipes
the cat litter we usually get, unscented
dog food, the salmon flavor 15lb bag
need baby formula, the sensitive stomach kind

labels.name: mixed_or_unspecified
labels.definition: Orders that span multiple product categories with no single dominant type, or that are too vague/incomplete to assign to any specific category above.
examples_of_edge_cases: just get whatever's needed for the week, you know what we usually buy
milk, toilet paper, dog food, and some apples
pick up stuff for dinner tonight, surprise me
same order as last time please

generation_personas: A busy working mother in her 30s texting quick grocery requests to her partner from her phone during lunch breaks, using abbreviations and no punctuation
An elderly retiree who dictates orders to a grocery delivery hotline over the phone, speaking in full formal sentences with occasional repetition and second-guessing
A college student ordering groceries via an app for the first time, casual tone, lots of slang, sometimes unsure of exact product names or brands
A professional chef restocking supplies for a small restaurant, writing precise, detailed orders with quantities and specific brand/cut preferences
A non-native English speaker who recently immigrated, writing simple broken-English sentences with some grammar mistakes but clear intent
A tech-savvy teenager ordering snacks and personal care items for themselves via a delivery app, using emojis and very short fragments
A pet owner and new parent juggling both baby and dog needs, writing rushed, run-on messages combining multiple categories at once
A frugal budget-conscious shopper who mentions prices, coupons, and asks for cheaper alternatives, writing in a somewhat anxious, detail-oriented tone
A person with limited literacy dictating a voice-to-text order that comes out with odd phrasing, missing words, and unconventional spelling
An office manager ordering bulk household and pantry supplies for a workplace break room, writing in a brisk, businesslike email format
